name: cli-tools
description: Profullstack's command-line tools as installable plugins — publish to the plain-HTML blog without getting a convention wrong.

plugins.name: tools
plugins.description: Install and manage the cli-tools command set: put every command on PATH, keep the checkout current, and wire up the moshcode pit aliases.

plugins.name: blog
plugins.description: Write, check and publish posts on the plain-HTML blog: next post number, smolweb-valid template, index listing and feed regeneration, with a lint that catches the mistakes that silently break RSS.

plugins.name: domain
plugins.description: Generate candidate product names from a sentence, find the ones you can actually register, and look one up in depth. Availability is read from the registry over RDAP, never guessed from DNS, so parked names and registrations with no nameservers are not mistaken for free.

plugins.name: ai
plugins.description: Ask a question and get an answer from the live web with the pages it came from, numbered to match the markers in the text, and read text aloud in a named voice. The paid APIs worth a command: a grounded answer you can check, and speech you can keep.

plugins.name: bo
plugins.description: BufferOverride from the terminal: wrap a failing command, keep what it printed with the environment that produced it, strip the secrets, and find the existing answer before asking. Answers declare the versions they are valid for, who or what wrote them, and how many people reproduced them.

plugins.name: myna
plugins.description: Post, schedule and read across 26 social networks from the terminal. Name the targets before anything goes out — the default is every account you have — queue for later, read back what landed and what failed, and draft copy the writer never publishes on its own. Accounts live in myna's own encrypted vault, not here.
